Starting or growing a business in wellness is exciting. Here is how to turn that enthusiasm into a successful venture.

Launching a private label supplement brand involves seven interconnected workstreams.        Get the first one wrong and the rest get harder. Get them all right and you have a business    that compounds.

Below is the framework our most successful partners use. It is built on 50 years of supplement industry experience and works whether you are launching with three SKUs or thirty.

params.content:
Let us take you to the next level.

Private labeling quality vitamins and supplements is easier than you think.

Start with the customer, not the catalog. The strongest supplement brands are built for a specific person with a specific goal, whether that is a busy parent, a competitive athlete, or a practitioner’s patient panel. When you know exactly who you serve, every later decision, from formula selection to packaging to price, gets easier and more consistent.

Craft a brand informed by your research. Master supplement branding that resonates with your target audience and reflects the values and quality of your supplements in your message, logo, and aesthetic. Consistency across platforms and materials builds a brand that consumers recognize and trust.

Strategize how to market your brand. With your brand identity in place, devise a marketing strategy. Below are the three highest-leverage channels for supplement brands.

Make your brand unmistakably yours. Private label supplements let you put your own identity on proven formulas, so spend your differentiation budget where customers actually look: the product name, the story on the label, and the unboxing experience. A focused brand that clearly signals who it is for will outsell a generic one that tries to speak to everybody.

Price for healthy margins from day one. Know your true per-unit cost at every order quantity, set a suggested retail price that leaves room for promotions and wholesale accounts, and understand how minimum order quantities change your landed cost. Private label supplements are appealing precisely because the profit margins can be strong when you price with intent instead of guessing.

Plan your sales channels before you launch. Decide early which channels fit your brand and your numbers: your own online store, Amazon, wholesale accounts with gyms, clinics, and retailers, and practitioner dispensaries. Each channel carries different pricing, packaging, and compliance expectations, and choosing deliberately keeps your margins and messaging consistent as you grow.

cards.content: Engage with your audience on their preferred social platforms. Share educational content, user testimonials, and promotions. Quality beats quantity. One thoughtful post per week beats five rushed ones.

cards.content: Create blog posts, videos, and infographics with valuable information about your supplements. Content builds search visibility, supports email and social, and converts skeptics over time.

Consumers want to know what they are putting into their bodies and how it will benefit them. Provide detailed product information including ingredient lists, benefits, and usage instructions.

Educational content positions your brand as a knowledgeable, credible resource. Consider creating blog posts, webinars, and e-books that explore the topics your customers actually care about. The brands that win long term are the ones customers turn to when they have a question, not just when they need a refill.

Educational content is also how new customers find you. When you answer the questions people search about ingredients, dosing, and results, you earn organic traffic that compounds over time and lowers what it costs to acquire each customer. Target the terms your buyers actually type, from broad topics down to specific product questions, and build a library that keeps working long after it is published.

Mix formats to reach different learners: in-depth guides, short social explainers, ingredient breakdowns, comparison articles, and email courses. Cite credible sources, be transparent about what a supplement can and cannot do, and keep every claim compliant. Trust is the currency of this category, and it is earned one honest, useful piece of content at a time.

Let your customers do some of the talking, too. Reviews, testimonials, and user-generated content are powerful social proof for supplement buyers who are understandably cautious. Make it easy for satisfied customers to share results, and feature that proof where new shoppers are deciding whether to trust your brand.

Email marketing remains one of the most effective channels for supplement brands. Your emails should feature value-rich content such as educational articles, brand updates, and special offers. Encourage visitors to sign up by offering incentives like discounts, exclusive content, or free guides.

Improve efficiency and consistency by automating campaigns: welcome emails, abandoned cart reminders, post-purchase follow-ups. Segment your list by interest, purchase history, or lifecycle stage so subscribers get messages relevant to where they are, not blasts to everyone.

Protect your sender reputation by keeping your list clean and honoring unsubscribes promptly, and mind supplement-specific compliance in every send: steer clear of disease claims and keep your language truthful. Set a cadence you can sustain, test subject lines and offers, and let performance rather than habit decide how often you show up in the inbox.

Lean on lifecycle flows that run without daily effort: a welcome series that introduces your brand story, replenishment reminders timed to when a bottle runs out, win-back campaigns for lapsed customers, and education that turns first-time buyers into repeat ones. Retention is where private label margins quietly compound.

params.headline: Customer-supplied artwork guidelines
params.subhead: Technical requirements for clients who are providing their own label artwork. Following these guidelines keeps your project on the 3-to-4-week production timeline and avoids rework.

params.content:
If you're supplying your own artwork,      here are the artwork submission requirements.

Customers who have their own designer or agency can supply finished label artwork directly. We'll review it against these technical requirements before sending it to print.

Most rework delays come from artwork that does not meet one of the five requirements below. Have your designer review this page before they start the file.

params.headline: Artwork must be submitted on our template.

params.content:
Our label templates provide the visual layout of your finished label. They are not optional. 

Changing or removing the template from the art file causes rework and extends your timeline.

The templates we provide show: where graphic elements vs. text can appear within the label area; what font sizes will print legibly and meet FDA regulatory requirements; what standardized information must be included and where it must be positioned relative to other elements.

Your designer must use our template as the base file.

params.headline: File format matters: vector only.

params.content:
To work on your label and prepare it for our printer, we need to receive your artwork in a vector format that our design team can re-open, edit, and resize without quality loss.

Accepted file formats: .eps (encapsulated PostScript) or .ai (Adobe Illustrator).

Do not send .pdf or .jpeg files. Those file types are not editable in our production workflow and will be rejected.

params.headline: Color must be set up in CMYK.

params.content:
There are two color formats: RGB and CMYK. Our printers require all files be set up as CMYK, which stands for the four primary colors of pigment: cyan, magenta, yellow, and black. These four inks are mixed in varying proportions to produce full-color print output.

RGB (red, green, blue) is used for digital displays: monitors, cameras, TV screens. RGB color values will not print accurately on a physical label.

If your files are set up in RGB, convert them to CMYK before sending. Color drift between RGB and CMYK can be significant and we cannot guarantee on-screen colors will match printed output if files arrive in RGB.

params.headline: Package all individual elements together.

params.content:
An art file is made up of many individual elements: fonts, graphics, logos, embedded images, and color swatches. All of these elements must be packaged together for the file to be editable and printable on our end.

Most design programs (Adobe Illustrator, InDesign) have a Package or Collect for Output function that bundles all linked assets, fonts, and color profiles into a single delivery folder. Use that function before sending. If anything is missing (a linked image, a font, a color swatch), the file cannot go to print.

params.headline: Decide whether to outline fonts.

params.content:
Outlining fonts converts text into vector objects. This means the text no longer requires the font file to be installed on another computer in order to display correctly.

Pros of outlining: appearance is preserved exactly when the file is sent to print. Eliminates the need to send your font files alongside the artwork.

Cons of outlining: any text edits required after the fact must be made by you and the file resent. Outlined text cannot be edited as text anymore.

If you're confident your label is final, outline fonts. If you anticipate revisions, leave fonts live and include the font files in your packaged delivery.
Our designers can review your file before submission and flag any technical issues. Catching problems before they hit print saves you days on the timeline.
params.headline: Questions on file prep?                    Talk to our design team.

params.subhead: Every batch of private label product passes through a multi-stage testing protocol covering identity, potency, contaminants, microbials, and stability. Quality is what your brand inherits when you partner with us.

Why testing protocols matter more than marketing claims.

Most supplement brands claim 'tested for purity and potency.' Few actually publish their testing protocols. Here's how testing works at our facility.

Every raw material is tested on receipt for identity (is this actually what was ordered) and quality (does it meet our specifications). Every batch is tested during production for potency. Every finished product is tested for contaminants, heavy metals, and microbial limits. Random samples go to third-party labs for verification.

params.subhead: THE BASICS OF PRIVATE LABEL SUPPLEMENTS

params.content:
WHAT ARE PRIVATE LABEL SUPPLEMENTS?

Private labeling is putting your brand on existing, high-quality nutritional supplement formulas with legal permission from their provider.

As the supplement landscape gears up to surpass a $1 trillion global ecosystem, generic formulations are taking a back seat. In 2026, consumers demand precise, data-driven wellness tailored to their unique biochemistry.  By offering custom, practitioner-endorsed fertility lines, you meet the modern patient's need for clinically validated, highly targeted egg-health support.

It allows healthcare practitioners and entrepreneurs to build a niche brand and grow their business with less liability risk because they may be partially protected by the supplier’s compliance and insurance umbrella policy.

Private labeling is an attractive option because research and development, legal considerations, marketing material, and FDA approved labels are provided by the supplement provider, enabling practitioners and business owners to reap the benefits without the time and expense of creating a new formula from scratch.

WHAT IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN PRIVATE LABEL AND WHITE LABEL SUPPLEMENTS?

The terms “private label” and “white label” are often used interchangeably. In the context of marketing supplements, there isn’t much difference between them, except a private label specifies the ingredients and concentration of nutrients included in the product. A white label, on the other hand, often means simply placing a brand logo on an otherwise generic product package.

SHOULD I SELL PRIVATE LABEL SUPPLEMENTS?

Selling private label supplements can significantly enhance brand recognition and patient loyalty. According to the 2024 CRN Consumer Survey, supplement users who purchase products directly from healthcare professionals report a median monthly expenditure of $100, indicating a strong level of trust and preference for obtaining supplements through their healthcare providers. Offering private label supplements under your own brand not only reinforces your professional credibility but also ensures patients receive products that meet your exacting standards.

When done correctly, it helps build trust among patients and lend credibility to your practice or business. When people see your brand is being used by friends or family, it helps reinforce your expertise in specific areas of health and wellness.

On top of this, private labeling can offer lucrative revenue opportunities.

For doctors, naturopaths, chiropractors, registered dietitians & nutritionists, and wellness coaches that sell supplements already, branding your own products adds a factor of exclusivity that can boost profitability.

You may already be re-selling high-quality supplements to your patients. However, many people are bargain hunters that may listen to your recommendation and search for a cheaper generic version of the product, rather than buy from you.

When you have your own unique blend of active ingredients designed to support a specific metabolic system, it’s harder for someone to hop on Amazon or go to Walmart and find an option they think will provide the same benefits, even though cheaper products often lack potency and include more fillers. Private labeling improves the likelihood your patients or client-base will buy directly from you.

By ensuring your patients purchase high-quality supplements, you can help them get the results they need. When they see results, their trust in your brand grows.

 

“When patients seek out lower-quality products online or at their neighborhood drug store, nobody wins. Private label supplements allow you to hone in on your clientele’s specific needs and demands and offer a selection of formulas you know and trust. Plus, they won’t be able to search for a lower price on the brand you are selling online, to under-cut your profit margin because you are selling your brand.”

– Mindy Elmadjian, Human Contract Manufacturing Business Leader at FoodScience LLC

HOW TO LAUNCH YOUR PRIVATE LABEL BRAND

Private labeling is a lucrative business. But it’s also increasingly competitive, so you’ll need to be organized and take a strategic approach. In this section, we will go over how to launch a private label brand in seven steps.


HOW DO I START A PRIVATE LABEL SUPPLEMENT BUSINESS?

1. Create a Checklist

2. Conduct Thorough Market Research

3. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

4. Select a Reputable Private Label Supplement Provider

5. Choose High-Demand, High-Quality Products

6. Design Professional Branding and Packaging

7. Establish Legal and Financial Foundations

8. Implement a Strategic Marketing Plan

9. Ensure Ongoing Compliance and Quality Control

10. Monitor Performance and Optimize Continuously

 

1. CREATE A CHECKLIST

Organization is critical when launching or expanding any business. If your organization plans on selling mass quantities through e-commerce sites like Amazon or physical retail spaces, start with a checklist that outlines all aspects of your business plan, including who will be doing what.

A few examples are: Who is my market? Who will design my label? What is my customer acquisition plan? If you are unsure about what questions to ask yourself and your team, we recommend the Checklist Manifesto by Atul Gawande.

2. EVALUATE YOUR MARKET

Evaluate your market to determine whether you should sell online, face to face, or both.

ONLINE:

1. Larger Market
2. Greater Revenue Potential
3. More Data

IN-PERSON:

1. Less Inventory
2. Greater Connection with Patients
3. Easier to Start

Understanding your market on a fundamental level will allow you to design a more effective course of action. This will determine everything from how to market your products to creating a fulfillment plan.

3. CHOOSE A HIGH-QUALITY SUPPLEMENT SUPPLIER

Tailoring your products to your practice, ideal patient, or business goals is important. For example, different healthcare providers specializing in functional medicine, hormone replacement, and chiropractic care often need vastly different supplements for their clients.

Focusing on your niche is the best path forward, allowing you to build trust and keep risk low.

If you’re an e-commerce vendor concerned with maximizing your margin, you’ll want to start with a few top-selling formulations and grow from there.

Once you have identified your market and a supplement formulation that provides a targeted solution to your market, it’s important to remember you can’t be everything to everyone. Start with one or two products to build your brand around. Once your brand has created a successful base of products, you could start expanding into others.

4. FIND THE RIGHT PRODUCTS TO PRIVATE LABEL

Focus on developing products that not only align with your practice or niche but also meet the needs of your client base. Traditionally successful categories include immune support, gut health, cognitive function, weight management, and supplements that support a healthy inflammatory response.*

Additionally, 2025 trends indicate increased demand for plant-based, allergen-free, and sustainably sourced supplements. Ensure your products address these preferences while providing high efficacy and bioavailability.

5. CREATE YOUR BRAND LOGO & LABEL

If you already have a logo for your practice or healthcare business, all you have to do is send it to your representative. They will make sure the design team incorporates your company logo into a beautiful, professional label.

If you don’t have branding already in place, you can work with our design team free of charge. Our team will work with you hand-in-hand to create a logo and label that represents your vision.

6. SET UP A LEGALLY ESTABLISHED BUSINESS

If you are a licensed healthcare professional, you probably already have a legally incorporated business. If not, register your business as a legal entity (e.g., LLC or corporation) to protect your personal assets. Obtain any required licenses and permits, particularly if you plan to sell supplements online or across state lines. Set up accounting systems that allow you to track sales, expenses, and profits accurately. Additionally, acquire insurance to protect your business from liability issues.

7. START SELLING YOUR NEWLY BRANDED SUPPLEMENTS!

At this point, you will be ready to receive your new supplement line in the mail and begin selling. If you are a sole proprietor or an established healthcare practitioner who wants to offer branded supplements directly to your patient base, starting a private label business is straightforward and quite affordable.

 

OUR PROCESS GETS YOU UP AND RUNNING IN THREE SIMPLE STEPS:

 

1. Select your formulas — choose a formulation from our extensive product line or talk with a sales consultant to discuss the best options to meet your goals.

 

2. Choose one of our design templates, provide us with your own logo/design, or work with our team to customize a label.

3. Receive your new private label supplements in the mail and start selling high-quality formulations to your patients or customers.

 

HOW LONG DO SUPPLEMENTS  TAKE TO DELIVER?

The process for first-orders takes roughly 10-12 days for label printing and product delivery. Subsequent orders typically take just three to five days.

For e-commerce retailers, we recommend maintaining extra inventory. Our minimum order quantity (MOQ) per product is only 36 units for Healthcare Practitioners (HCPs); 72 units for non-HCPs; and 144 units for retailers selling on Amazon.

Running out of products on e-commerce sites can negatively impact your brand. According to AMZ Advisors, when you run out of stock, you risk losing rank, sales, trust, and a competitive edge. On the other hand, practitioners who see patients face-to-face or through telemedicine have more flexibility with inventory. Maintaining stock isn’t as challenging, especially since they can usually get a new order shipped quickly.

CAN I RELABEL A PRODUCT AND SELL IT?

Simply buying a product and repackaging it with your own label without consent is not the same as private labeling. It would put you at risk for legal action for multiple instances of infringement.

With our low minimum order quantities, you could have your first shipment of branded supplements entirely set up and ready to sell for less than five-hundred dollars.

Some providers have a reputation for including hidden fees or additional costs related to developing the labels – so it’s a good idea to ask your provider for a detailed explanation of all expenses involved.

Our private labeling services include label design, production, and help with identifying products that will best suit your business. Instead of charging service or label fees, we’ve built all of these features into our minimums to keep the process streamlined and affordable.

Additional offerings available at no charge include digital imaging of your bottles and branded product sell sheets for your office, website or online sales.

WHAT IS THE MARKUP ON SUPPLEMENTS?

Marking up supplements is a judgement call that depends on your niche and how well-marketed your line is. A markup of around 100% is standard. If your cost comes down to $10.00 per unit, you might sell it for $20.00 and find your sweet spot.

Some highly successful private label brands have managed to market themselves so well that they effectively sell their products for three to four times the cost.

 

MEETING PRIVATE LABEL SUPPLEMENT SAFETY & QUALITY STANDARDS

In 2026, consumers are increasingly prioritizing supplement quality, with a significant number indicating that third-party testing certifications influence their purchasing decisions. For instance, a study among collegiate athletes found that over 90% believed it was essential to know if a supplement was third-party tested. Additionally, research shows consumers are willing to pay more for nutraceuticals associated with high safety standards, highlighting the value placed on transparency and testing. Partnering 

with providers who provide transparent testing results and hold certifications from organizations like NSF International or USP can enhance consumer trust and product credibility.

WHAT QUALIFIES AS A SUPPLEMENT?

In the United States, dietary supplements are regulated under the Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act (DSHEA) of 1994. Under this framework, a supplement is any product intended to add nutritional value to the diet, taken by mouth, that contains one or more of the following: vitamins, minerals, herbs or botanicals, amino acids, enzymes, or concentrates derived from these ingredients.

Supplements are not drugs. They cannot claim to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease. What they can do is support general health and wellness, and that distinction matters both legally and practically for your brand.

The category is broader than most people expect. Capsules, tablets, soft gels, liquids, powders, chewables, and gummies can all qualify as dietary supplements depending on their ingredients and intended use. So can collagen peptides, probiotics, omega-3s, and adaptogens like ashwagandha.

What does not qualify: products making drug claims, foods marketed primarily as conventional food, and anything delivered intravenously.

For private label brands, understanding this boundary is foundational. It determines what you can say on your label, how your products must be fulfilled, and what regulatory requirements apply before your product ever reaches a customer.

DO NUTRITIONAL SUPPLEMENTS NEED FDA APPROVAL?

Nutritional supplements and vitamins are not governed by the FDA. The Food and Drug Administration does not have authority over whether or not vitamins and supplements can be sold. However, like any other food product, supplements must be compliant with the FDA’s regulations regarding labeling and manufacturing.

Provisions, laboratory production controls, and distribution guidelines for supplements and cosmetics are regulated under the Food Drug and Cosmetic Act (Code of Federal Regulations Title 21 Section 111). Current Good Manufacturing Practices (CGMPs) required under CFR-21-111 ensure testing is done on every raw material in a supplement. These tests measure purity, potency, identity, and contaminants in order to prove the product meets all standards put in place. cGMPs also provide a statistically valid method for substantiating label claims on finished products.

WHO IS RESPONSIBLE FOR MAKING SURE A SUPPLEMENT IS SAFE?

Since vitamins and nutritional supplements do not need FDA approval for sales, the onus is on the provider's CGMP compliance. The provider must make sure that the products are safe before taking them to market for distribution.

This is one reason why private labeling supplements is a wise route; an established private label provider ensures all products are safe and ready for market.  As a private label customer, you have protection from associated liabilities as long as you follow our labeling guidelines.

HOW DO YOU KNOW IF VITAMINS ARE GOOD QUALITY?

The best way to determine the quality of a supplement is to evaluate the company you are purchasing from and ask questions.

A FEW THINGS TO LOOK FOR DURING THE VETTING PROCESS:

• Is the supplement provider FDA registered?
• Does the provider have an up-to-date Current Good Manufacturing Practices (CGMP) certification?
• Do they have on-site regulatory and quality control departments?
• Does clinical research back their ingredients?
• Did doctors or nutritional experts create the formulas?
• Does the provider employ 3rd-party testing?

If you are a doctor, naturopath, or licensed healthcare practitioner of any sort, you don’t want to give your patients anything you wouldn’t take yourself. Verifying supplement quality is easy. Just ask the private label provider for compliance documentation. You can also do a Google search for product recalls and truth-in-labeling violations. Additionally, you should look for silver or gold CGMP certification.

Embracing private label supplements in 2026 positions your practice at the forefront of the health and wellness industry. By offering high-quality, customized products, you not only meet the evolving needs of your patients but also establish a sustainable revenue stream that supports the growth and success of your business.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need an existing logo to start a private label supplement line?

No. If you already have a logo for your practice or healthcare business, you can provide it to your representative for use on your label. If you do not yet have branding in place, you can work with the design team to create a professional logo and label that fits your vision.

Do I need a legally established business to sell private label supplements?

In many cases, yes. If you are not already operating through a legally established business, it is generally wise to register as a legal entity, obtain any licenses or permits that may apply, and set up accounting and insurance appropriate for your business model.

How does our private label process work?

The process is designed to be simple. You select your formulas, choose a label direction or provide your own branding, and then receive your finished private label supplements so you can begin offering them to patients or customers.

How long does it take to receive a private label supplement order?

First orders typically take about 10 to 12 days for label printing and delivery. After the first order, turnaround is usually much faster, with many reorders shipping in roughly three to five days.

What are the minimum order quantities for private label supplements?

Minimums vary by customer type. MOQ is 36 units per product for healthcare practitioners,                        72 units for non-HCPs, and 144 units for retailers selling on Amazon.

Can I relabel an existing product and sell it as my own?

Simply buying a product and relabeling it without permission is not the same as private labeling.                  A legitimate private label program provides authorized branding, label production, and a compliant process for selling products under your own brand.

Are there additional costs beyond the product minimums?

Some providers may charge separate design or service fees, which is why it is important to ask for a full explanation of costs. Our process includes label design, production, and product-selection support within our minimums to keep everything streamlined.

What additional private label support options are available?

Additional options may include digital product imaging for online sales, branded marketing materials     such as sell sheets and product information.

What qualifies as a supplement?

A supplement is generally understood as a product intended to supplement the diet and may include vitamins, minerals, herbs, amino acids, enzymes, or other dietary ingredients. For business and compliance purposes, products should also align with applicable labeling and manufacturing regulations.

Do nutritional supplements need FDA approval?

Nutritional supplements are not approved by the FDA in the same way as drugs. However, supplement products still need to comply with FDA regulations related to labeling, manufacturing, and current good manufacturing practices.

Who is responsible for supplement safety?

The provider is responsible for making sure supplement products are safe and compliant before they are brought to market. This is one reason many businesses choose established private label providers with quality systems already in place.

How can I evaluate supplement quality before choosing a provider?

A strong vetting process includes reviewing whether the provider is FDA registered, follows current good manufacturing practices, maintains regulatory and quality control systems, uses third-party testing, and provides documentation that supports compliance and product quality.

What is a typical markup on supplements?

Markup depends on your niche, positioning, and how your line is marketed. While a standard markup of 100% is common, some brands may price at a significantly higher multiple depending on brand strength and demand.

Why do safety and quality standards matter so much in private label supplements?

Consumers increasingly value transparency, testing, and documented quality standards. Working with a provider that emphasizes compliance, testing, and clear documentation can help support consumer confidence and brand credibility.

items.answer: A private label supplement is a pre-formulated dietary supplement produced by a manufacturer (us) and sold under your brand name. You don't formulate it, you don't manufacture it, and you don't run quality testing. You select from existing formulations, design your label, and we produce finished inventory ready to ship under your brand.
items.question: What is a private label supplement, exactly?

items.answer: The terms are used interchangeably by most people. Technically, white label refers to generic products that anyone can rebrand identically. Private label refers to formulations and packaging that are customized for a specific brand. In our world, the practical difference is small: you get to customize the label design (and optionally the packaging) regardless of which term you use.
items.question: What is the difference between private label and white label?

items.answer: Most clients launch a 3-5 SKU line for under $15,000 in initial inventory, including label design. items.question: How much does it cost to start a supplement brand with private labeling?

items.answer: Three things matter most. First: pick a real niche and audience, not a generic 'wellness' play. Second: understand DSHEA labeling rules (structure-function claims, supplement facts panels, disclaimers) before you finalize labels. Third: plan distribution. Direct-to-consumer Shopify is the most accessible channel; retail and wholesale need additional positioning work. We help you think through all three during onboarding.
items.question: What are the most important things to know before launching a private label supplement brand?

items.answer: Standard supplement retail pricing follows a 4-5x markup over cost-of-goods for DTC and 2-3x for wholesale. Premium positioning supports higher markups. We give you transparent SKU-level cost data so you can price intelligently for your channel and audience.
items.question: How do I price my private label supplements?

items.answer: In the U.S., you don't need a license to sell dietary supplements, but you must comply with FDA labeling rules (DSHEA), follow good manufacturing practices on your distribution side, and register with FDA if you import or manufacture certain products. We handle the manufacturing-side compliance. Your business-side compliance (state business licenses, sales tax registration, claims review) is your responsibility, and we point you to resources.
items.question: Do I need any licenses or certifications to sell private label supplements?

items.answer: Yes. Many of our private label clients sell on Amazon. You will need to register your brand in Amazon Brand Registry, ensure your labels comply with Amazon's supplement category requirements (which are stricter than basic FDA rules), and meet their barcoding requirements. We help you understand these during onboarding.
